Raj, R., Suman, R., Ghandehariun, S., Kumar, A. and Tiwari, M.K. (2016). A techno-economic assessment of the liquefied natural gas (LNG) production facilities in Western Canada. Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments, 18, 140-152. DOI 10.1016/j.seta.2016.10.005.

Locators are printed journal page numbers (140-152). Bottom-up cost model of a 10 MTPA two-train C3MR LNG plant at Kitimat BC (the registered to-get row cited this as Ghandehariun et al.; first author is Raj). Main file: whole-plant capex ($1200/tpa), opex ($48/tpa = 4% of capex), amortized liquefaction cost ($4.4/GJ = 3.6 + 0.8), discount rate and life, plus installed equipment costs for amine sweetening, molecular-sieve dehydration, NGL recovery and the C3MR liquefaction section. All US dollars base year 2014 as stated. Traps: (1) the $1.9 bn in the abstract is total investment = 2.36 x on-site equipment cost of $801 M, not the plant capex; the $1200/tpa (about $12 bn) is a separate figure, and the Table 6 labor items (1.9 + 3.7 + 6.7 + 2 bn) do not reconcile with either; (2) plant life 25 years in text and Table 6, 20 years in Eq. 12; (3) Table 4 labels feed temperature and pressure swapped (6.76 MPa/311 K printed as MPa and K in wrong rows) and heat loads printed in W instead of MW; (4) storage tanks 58% of on-site cost. No energy-per-tonne or emissions are printed; compressor power (141.86 MW per 5 MTPA train) is in _other-values. Gas turbines and electricity are on-site gas-fired (no grid).
